title.narrative: Safeguarding Children and Restoring Dignity: Integrated WASH, Nutrition, and Child Protection Response in Bama and Damboa LGAs of Borno State

description.narrative: ltpgtThis integrated project, led by the Centre for Advocacy, Transparency and Accountability Initiative (CATAI) in partnership with the Unique Care and Support Foundation (CASFOD), aims to respond to the escalating humanitarian needs in Bama and Damboa LGAs of Borno State during the 2025 lean season. These areas remain among the most crisis-affected in Nigeria’s BAY states due to prolonged conflict, mass displacement, food insecurity, and service disruption. The project will deliver a comprehensive, multisectoral package of life-saving interventions across Nutrition, Child Protection, and WASH sectors, targeting 23,058 direct beneficiaries with a strong focus on women, children, and persons with disabilities.ltbrgtCATAI will lead WASH interventions in Bama and child protection services in Damboa, while CASFOD will implement all nutrition activities in Damboa. This division of labor leverages each organization’s comparative advantage and deep community presence. Interventions are designed to be gender-responsive, age-appropriate, inclusive, and locally driven, contributing to improved nutrition outcomes, reduced protection risks, and enhanced access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene.ltbrgtIn Nutrition, 9,000 children aged 0–59 months will be screened for acute malnutrition using the Family MUAC approach, with 600 children treated for SAM and 600 for MAM through OTP, SC, and TSFP services. An additional 500 pregnant and breastfeeding women/caregivers will receive skilled Maternal, Infant and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) counselling, while 60 peer support groups will be established to sustain IYCF practices. Community Health Workers and Nutrition Mobilizers will be trained on IMAM protocols and GBV/PSEA to ensure quality and safety in service delivery.ltbrgtThe Child Protection component will provide comprehensive case management services to 150 children at risk of abuse, neglect, exploitation, or separation. This includes direct support, referrals, and psychosocial support through child-friendly spaces. Additionally, 7,000 individuals will be reached with awareness sessions on child protection, GBV, PSEA, and referral pathways. One community-based child protection committee will be established and trained to ensure local ownership and sustainability.ltbrgtWASH interventions will include the rehabilitation of latrines, establishment of 10 trained WASH committees, and distribution of 600 WASH kits and 400 dignity kits to vulnerable households. Hygiene promotion campaigns will target 9,000 individuals with behavior change messages focused on handwashing, water safety, and menstrual hygiene management. All infrastructure will be designed with gender and disability considerations, including lighting and secure locks for latrines and ramps for accessibility.ltbrgtThe project embeds accountability and sustainability through community engagement, feedback mechanisms (including toll-free lines and suggestion boxes), and integration with local structures. Participatory safety audits and inclusive design processes will ensure services meet the specific needs of women, children, and persons with disabilities. Both partners are national NGOs, advancing the NHF’s localization goals and leveraging local capacities for a context-driven, efficient, and scalable humanitarian response.ltbrgtAligned with the 2025 Nigeria Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) and the NHF First Standard Allocation Strategy, the project contributes directly to Strategic Objective 1 by delivering timely, life-saving assistance to the most vulnerable populations, reducing excess mortality and morbidity while reinforcing community resilience and dignity.lt/pgt
